resources.string: This device\'s channel shows once the master mouse is here.
Sends the master mouse and the devices that move along to that channel. The flockswitch tile in Quick Settings does the same.
No mouse with the wheel mode button found yet.
They move to the same channel as the master mouse.
This mouse does not have this button
Channel %d is this device\'s, so it cannot be chosen.
Hold the button, move the mouse and let go to switch as set for that direction. While any direction is on, the pointer stays still as long as the button is held.
Settings are kept per computer: choose on each one where its button sends everything. The channel numbers must mean the same computer on every device (e.g. 1 = Windows PC, 2 = Mac, 3 = this tablet).
Keep at least one button on. To stop switching, turn off “Switch with mouse buttons”.
flockswitch may not use the receiver yet
Allow flockswitch to access the Logitech receiver. Typing and pointing keep working; flockswitch only uses the receiver\'s own settings channel.
Android\'s own Logitech driver is using this receiver, so flockswitch left it alone to keep the mouse and keyboard working. Unplug the receiver and plug it in again to retry.
Plug a Logitech Bolt or Unifying receiver into this device (a USB-C or OTG adapter may be needed), and pair the mouse and keyboard with it on a channel of their own.
Android needs the “Nearby devices” permission before flockswitch can keep running in the background.
Notifications are off: the background notification with the channel buttons cannot be shown.
Also looks for Logitech devices connected to this device over Bluetooth, without a receiver.
Allow “Nearby devices” to use Bluetooth devices.
When a new version is found, it is downloaded, checked (SHA256) and installed. If Android asks for confirmation, a notification lets you know.
Version %s is ready: confirm the install in Android\'s prompt
Version %s did not match its SHA256 checksum, so it was not installed
New version ready to install — tap to install
Bugs, errors, ideas — anything. Your mail app opens with the app version, device and recent log filled in.

Rest the mouse pointer against an edge of the screen for a moment and the group and the master mouse go to the channel set for that side. No network: each computer watches its own screen. Works while the master mouse is on this device.

To watch the screen edges flockswitch needs “Display over other apps”: thin invisible strips along the edges notice the pointer, and the countdown is drawn on top of what is on the screen. No input is taken.

Only a Logitech mouse with a haptic motor (currently the MX Master 4) vibrates. Test plays it once at the chosen strength while that mouse is on this device. The strength goes to the mouse when applied; the mouse forgets it when it loses power, so it is applied again whenever the mouse is here. “Options+” leaves the Logi Options+ setting alone.

The wait does not start until Control is down, even with the pointer at the edge. With flockswitch\'s accessibility service on, letting go calls it off at once; without it Android reports the key only as the pointer moves.
Turn on the accessibility service so the key counts even while the pointer rests.
When the mouse arrives from another computer

Android tells an app where the pointer is only through an accessibility service, and only by holding the mouse back from other apps while it listens. So flockswitch listens for just one event: the highlight appears at your next mouse movement, within 5 seconds, and stays where the pointer was then. The notification has a button for it too.
Find the cursor needs the accessibility service.
Android gives apps the mouse pointer\'s position only from Android 14 on. On this version only the preview can be shown.

Used only for flockswitch settings you turn on. Sees the keyboard to know whether Control is held and to catch Ctrl+Alt+L; every other key passes through untouched and nothing is stored or sent. Reads the mouse pointer\'s position once, at the next movement after you ask to find the cursor.
Puts every setting back to how it started.
Android tells an app about a keyboard\'s keys and the mouse pointer only through an accessibility service. The top and bottom edges, the Control option and Find the cursor need it.
It does not read the screen. It only looks at Control and Ctrl+Alt+L, and stores or sends nothing. You can turn it off on the same screen at any time.
1. Open the accessibility settings below, turn on flockswitch and allow it. On Samsung phones it is under \'Installed apps\'.
2. If a \'Restricted setting\' message appears, tap OK, open App info below, and choose \'Allow restricted settings\' from the ⋮ menu at the top right. Then do step 1 again.
3. Come back here to see below whether it is on.
Needed to switch at the screen edge and to show effects.
Needed for the top and bottom edges, the Control option and Find the cursor.
The status and navigation bars cover the top and bottom edges, so those two need the accessibility service.
